summary: No. With scikit-learn defaults and an identical preprocessing pipeline, the random forest reached a mean stratified 5-fold CV ROC-AUC of 0.9022 versus 0.9051 for logistic regression, a difference of -0.0029 (RF - LogReg) in favour of logistic regression; RF was higher in 1/5 folds (paired t-test p=0.0229). The gap is small relative to the ~0.0042 between-fold SD, so the two default models perform very similarly.
primary_metric_name: ROC-AUC difference (RF - LogReg), mean over stratified 5-fold CV
methodological_choices: Both classifiers left at scikit-learn defaults as specified (RandomForestClassifier(): 100 trees, unlimited depth; LogisticRegression(): lbfgs, L2, C=1.0, max_iter=100). Identical preprocessing for both, fitted inside each CV fold via a Pipeline to avoid leakage: numerics median-imputed and StandardScaler-scaled; categoricals mode-imputed and one-hot encoded (handle_unknown='ignore'). Missing values ('?' in workclass, occupation, native-country) were imputed rather than dropped. Exact duplicate rows were dropped (52 rows). fnlwgt (a survey sampling weight) was kept as an ordinary predictor rather than dropped or used as a sample weight. Target encoded as >50K = positive (23.9% prevalence); no class-imbalance handling (no class_weight, no resampling) since ROC-AUC is threshold-free and prevalence-insensitive. Validation: StratifiedKFold(n_splits=5, shuffle=True, random_state=42), the SAME folds for both models, so the comparison is paired; significance via a paired t-test on the 5 fold AUCs (only 5 correlated observations, so treat the p-value as indicative). RF used its default random seed (unseeded). Sensitivity checks: leaving numerics unscaled for logistic regression gives LR AUC 0.7175 (diff +0.1847); raising max_iter to 1000 so lbfgs fully converges gives LR AUC 0.9051 (diff -0.0029); repeating the whole 5-fold CV under 5 different fold seeds gives a mean diff of -0.0037 (sd 0.0008), and the sign of the difference was stable across those seeds. Note this compares the two DEFAULT configurations only; either model could move with tuning (e.g. RF depth/min_samples_leaf, LR regularisation or feature engineering such as binning capital-gain), so the result should not be read as a general statement about the two model classes.
